theorems.theorem_title: Physical wanted scanning and the complete fast and hybrid program assemblies
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines the ascending wanted-slot scan, its counter predicate, retained consumer data, and the concrete selected-color, fast-driver, and hybrid programs. For natural slot masses $m_i$, hit predicates $H_i$, threshold $\tau$, and prefix length $N$, acceptance is defined by
$$\operatorname{Accepted}(N)\iff\tau<\sum_{i<N}m_i\ \lor\ \exists i<N,\ H_i.$$
The scan body returns immediately after a successful prefix; its counter contract records the first accepted prefix on success. For input length $n$, value bound $U$, fixed magnitude exponent $\kappa$, and the chosen cutoff $c_\kappa$, the hybrid assembly selects the original-triple fallback when $n<c_\kappa$ or $U>n^\kappa$, and the composed fast driver otherwise. Resource and time functions accompany these assemblies.

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
namespace Light
end Light
namespace ThreeSum.LightReportingWantedDispatch
end ThreeSum.LightReportingWantedDispatch
namespace ThreeSum.SharedTraversalCosts
end ThreeSum.SharedTraversalCosts


/-!
# Ascending physical wanted scan with immediate successful return

The recursive prefix runs before slot n-1. A positive prefix result returns
immediately; otherwise exactly the next physical slot is dispatched. The
counter is the exact mass of the executed prefix, including the first slot
whose guard or original-value test succeeds.
-/

namespace ThreeSum.LightReportingWantedScan

open Light Finset SharedTraversalCosts LightReportingWantedDispatch

set_option maxHeartbeats 2600000
set_option maxRecDepth 24000

def Accepted (mass : ℕ→ℕ) (hit : ℕ→Prop) (threshold n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  threshold<prefixMass mass n ∨ ∃ i<n, hit i






























def Counter (mass : ℕ→ℕ) (hit : ℕ→Prop) (threshold count counter : ℕ)
    (result : ℤ) (μ : ℕ→ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∃ k≤count, μ counter=(prefixMass mass k : ℤ) ∧
    (result=0 → k=count) ∧
    (result=1 → Accepted mass hit threshold k ∧ ∀ i<k, ¬Accepted mass hit threshold i)

def time (stepTime : ℕ→ℕ) : ℕ→ℕ
  | 0 => 30
  | n+1 => time stepTime n+stepTime n+300

def body (pSelf pDispatch : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  .ite ((Light.Cond.lt (k 0) (v 0)))
    ((Light.Stmt.seq
       (.call pSelf
         [(Light.Expr.op Light.Op.sub) (v 0) (k 1), v 1, v 2, v 3, v 4, v 5, v 6,
           v 7, v 8, v 9, v 10, v 11, v 12, v 13, v 14, v 15, v 16, v 17, v 18, v 19,
           v 20, v 21, v 22]
         23)
       (.ite (Light.Cond.lt (k 0) (v 23)) (.set 0 (k 1))
         (.call pDispatch
           [(Light.Expr.op Light.Op.sub) (v 0) (k 1), v 1, v 2, v 3, v 4, v 5, v 6,
             v 7, v 8, v 9, v 10, v 11, v 12, v 13, v 14, v 15, v 16, v 17, v 18,
             v 19, v 20, v 21, v 22]
           0))))
    (.set 0 (k 0))

def program : Program := LightReportingWantedDispatch.program++[body 152 151]



































































end ThreeSum.LightReportingWantedScan

end

    (hsA : A.Pairwise (· < ·)) (hsB : B.Pairwise (· < ·)) (hsC : C.Pairwise (· < ·)) : ℕ :=
  (BandRawA.sortedRecords A B C (bandSize n) (bandSize_pos n) hsA hsB hsC).length

def count (n : ℕ) (A B C : List ℤ)
    (hsA : A.Pairwise (· < ·)) (hsB : B.Pairwise (· < ·)) (hsC : C.Pairwise (· < ·)) : ℕ :=
  WantedResidueKeys.total (radix n)
    (LightGuardedWanted.left (EncodedColorPrimeReadyData.selected n A B C hsA hsB hsC)
      (incidences n A B C hsA hsB hsC))
    (LightGuardedWanted.right (microHalf (inputBits n)) (blockCount (inputBits n)))
    (3*(incidences n A B C hsA hsB hsC).length)
    (LightGuardedWanted.totalKeys (microHalf (inputBits n)) (blockCount (inputBits n)))
    (shift n A B C hsA hsB hsC)

def config (free n : ℕ) (A B C : List ℤ)
    (hsA : A.Pairwise (· < ·)) (hsB : B.Pairwise (· < ·)) (hsC : C.Pairwise (· < ·)) :
    LightReportingWantedDispatch.Config where
  layoutHeader := counter free n A B C hsA hsB hsC+4
  J := blockCount (inputBits n)
  h := microHalf (inputBits n)
  K := LightSwitchDepth.depth (blockCount (inputBits n))
  N := (incidences n A B C hsA hsB hsC).length
  NB := B.length
  NC := C.length
  cover := EncodedColorPipelineData.coverBase free n
  counter := counter free n A B C hsA hsB hsC
  pairs := LightWantedSetup.pairBase
    (EncodedColorPipelineData.wantedHeader free n (incidences n A B C hsA hsB hsC).length)
    (3*(incidences n A B C hsA hsB hsC).length)
    (LightGuardedWanted.totalKeys (microHalf (inputBits n)) (blockCount (inputBits n))) (radix n)
  layerCount := OutputDecodeRecords.layerCount (microHalf (inputBits n))
  scheduleSize := GlobalEncoding.scheduleSize (microHalf (inputBits n))
  masks := LightCoverKeys.afterCover (EncodedColorPipelineData.coverBase free n) (microHalf (inputBits n))
  vals := EncodedColorLayout.vals free n (bandSize n)
  owners := LightBandRawA.ownerBase (EncodedColorLayout.vals free n (bandSize n))
    (recordCount n A B C hsA hsB hsC) (bandSize n)
  records := EncodedColorLayout.rec free n (bandSize n)
  pair := EncodedColorPipelineData.controls free n A B C hsA hsB hsC+3
  bank := EncodedColorPipelineData.bankHeader free n A B C hsA hsB hsC
  srcB := EncodedColorLayout.bv free n
  srcC := EncodedColorLayout.cv free n
  report := reportBase free n A B C hsA hsB hsC
  modulus := radix n










theorem count_read {μ : ℕ→ℤ} {free n : ℕ}
    {color : Coloring.Parameter (inputBits n+1)} {x : Fin n→ℤ} {A B C : List ℤ}
    {hsA : A.Pairwise (· < ·)} {hsB : B.Pairwise (· < ·)} {hsC : C.Pairwise (· < ·)}
    (H : EncodedColorPipelineData.Stored μ free n color x A B C hsA hsB hsC) :

      (count n A B C hsA hsB hsC : ℤ) := H.wanted.1

theorems.theorem_title: Wanted-slot dispatch, composed color pipelines, and machine resource budgets
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines wanted-slot configurations and the program calls for layout construction, decoding, source selection, and guarded reporting. It composes the selected-color pipeline with shared reporting setup and assigns word, space, and depth requirements to parameter initialization, preprocessing, dense counters, scans, and drivers. For natural input size $n$, set $M=2^{2048(\operatorname{log2}(n)+1)}$, with $\operatorname{log2}(0)=0$. The defined query and wanted envelopes are
$$E_{\mathrm{query}}=100(M+1)^6,\qquad E_{\mathrm{wanted}}=10000(M+1)^{10}.$$
Additional cost functions specify preprocessing, per-color work, and the hybrid branch selected by size and input-magnitude guards.

theorems.theorem_title: Complete shared-bank rows, retained color data, and frontier traversal
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines the physical order of shared reporting rows. With $n_B,n_C$ source-band counts, occurrence index $s$, and band indices $i,j$, the row rank is
$$\operatorname{rank}(s,i,j)=(s n_B+i)n_C+j.$$
The completed-row predicate requires all valid rows below a processed rank to contain their level catalogs. Header and access definitions locate the full metadata slab and payloads. Retained pipeline records connect normalized color inputs, chosen primes, cover data, wanted pairs, and source banks. Program bodies compose complete bank construction, positive-frontier expansion, level traversal, and reporting setup; accompanying definitions specify traversal costs and finite resource envelopes.

theorems.theorem_title: Shared reporting cells, level layouts, and wanted-query initialization
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines shared reporting-bank cells, their metadata and table predicates, and the per-level switch and box cutoff. For half-size $h$, block count $J$, and width $W=512hJ$, the common query spans are
$$\operatorname{maskSpan}=2^W,\qquad\operatorname{workSpan}=(W+1)^2+8(W+1)+8.$$
Program bodies assemble source-band hosts and control records, guarded wanted-pair construction, catalog batches, level queries, initialization, and child expansion. Original wanted labels retain incidence position, lift, and complete output identity. Source-normalization predicates and finite cost expressions connect these layouts to the selected-color inputs and the larger shared-bank construction.

theorems.theorem_title: Persistent cover and source catalogs, level interfaces, and terminal programs
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines retained cover/key data, occurrence-indexed source catalogs, their physical headers, and the programs that construct them. A suffix table of width $V$ and cutoff $c$ has stride
$$\operatorname{stride}(V,c)=(V+1)\sum_{a=0}^{\min(V,c)}\binom{V}{a}.$$
Reporting interfaces collect five-field catalog descriptors, sorted packed-index storage, pointer arrays, source-stage tables, address bounds, and scratch requirements. Further bodies compose prefix-index construction, catalog queries, suffix-catalog setup, and terminal scans over stored frontiers. Local-cover metadata and source-control layouts provide the concrete addresses and parameters consumed by these programs.

namespace ThreeSum.ReportingHostLevelData

structure Catalog where
  t : ℕ
  boxCut : ℕ
  boxBase : ℕ
  indexBase : ℕ
  ptrBase : ℕ

/-- The fields actually consumed by the level machine, including the computed
prefix count. The box base remains a semantic ownership bound. -/
def Catalog.record (D : Catalog) (h k : ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  [D.t,D.boxCut,D.indexBase,D.ptrBase,count h k]

variable {α β γ : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
  [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]

structure Sources {h J : ℕ} (μ : ℕ→ℤ) (pMod shift : ℤ) (B : Finset β) (C : Finset γ)
    (b : β→ℤ) (c : γ→ℤ) (q : GlobalOutput h J) (baseL baseR : ℕ) : Prop where
  left : LightZetaStages.StoredThrough μ baseL (sourceCut h J) (leftSource pMod B b q) (width h J)
  right : LightZetaStages.StoredThrough μ baseR (sourceCut h J) (rightSource pMod shift C c q) (width h J)

structure Stored {h J k : ℕ} (μ : ℕ→ℤ) (D : Catalog) (hk : k≤J)
    (pMod shift : ℤ) (B : Finset β) (C : Finset γ) (b : β→ℤ) (c : γ→ℤ)
    (q : GlobalOutput h J) : Prop where
  index : ∃ S : List ℤ, Seg μ D.indexBase S ∧
    S.Perm (ReportingHostPackedCatalog.codes (ReportingHostPackedCatalog.prefixKey h J k) (count h k)) ∧
    S.Pairwise (· ≤ ·)
  pointers : SegN μ D.ptrBase (List.ofFn fun i : Fin (count h k) =>
    D.boxBase+i.val*stride (suffixStage J (512*h) k) D.boxCut)
  boxes : ∀ i<count h k, LightBoxStages.StoredThrough μ
    (D.boxBase+i*stride (suffixStage J (512*h) k) D.boxCut) D.boxCut
    (leafWeight (block_fit hk) (leftSource pMod B b q) (rightSource pMod shift C c q)
      (suffixStage J (512*h) k) (preL h J k i) (preR h J k i)) (suffixStage J (512*h) k)

structure Bounds (h J k : ℕ) (D : Catalog) (baseL baseR stop : ℕ) : Prop where
  left : baseL+(width h J+1)*downsetCap (width h J) (sourceCut h J)≤stop
  right : baseR+(width h J+1)*downsetCap (width h J) (sourceCut h J)≤stop
  index : D.indexBase+count h k≤stop
  pointers : D.ptrBase+count h k≤stop
  boxes : D.boxBase+count h k*stride (suffixStage J (512*h) k) D.boxCut≤stop

structure Scratch (lim : Limits) (h J k : ℕ) (D : Catalog) (bCard cCard maskBase work : ℕ) : Prop where
  masks : maskBase+LightSparseQuery.queryItems (residualSize h J k) D.t≤work
  space : work+1+tableSize (width h J)+(width h J+1)≤lim.space
  powers : work+(2*width h J+2)≤lim.space
  emod : work+(Nat.log 2 (LightReportingCatalogLookup.valueBound (width h J) (count h k)+1)+2)≤lim.space
  word : (((width h J+1)*2^(width h J+1) : ℕ) : ℤ)≤lim.word
  lookup : (LightReportingCatalogLookup.word (width h J) (count h k) : ℤ)≤lim.word
  values : (LightSparseQuery.magnitudeBound (suffixStage J (512*h) k) (suffixStage J (512*h) k)
    (residualSize h J k) D.t bCard cCard : ℤ)≤lim.word
  t : D.t≤residualSize h J k+1
  cut : D.boxCut≤residualSize h J k
  flags : residualSize h J k-D.t≤D.boxCut


























































end ThreeSum.ReportingHostLevelData

end

theorems.theorem_title: Suffix-query composition, retained source batches, and packed prefix records
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines the explicit-subset and canonical-box portions of suffix queries, their signed sums and local tables, and terminal mask enumeration and endpoint preparation. For $N$ physical prefix records with natural keys $k_i$, their packed codes are
$$\operatorname{code}_i=k_i(N+1)+i\qquad(0\le i<N).$$
The original record index occupies the low digit. Further definitions assemble local-cover setup, retained left/right source-bank batches, and common-prime construction for selected colors. Wanted-workspace layouts specify counter, decoding, access, and frontier regions, while cumulative root-mass and terminal-cost functions describe the quantities used by later traversal contracts.

theorems.theorem_title: Parameter initialization, source hosts, and assembled search drivers
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines composed Light programs for parameter initialization, local-cover construction, balanced wanted-pair joins, source-band catalogs, color normalization, common-prime minimization, and sparse queries. Dense setup stores
$$
[0,CS,C,S],
$$
where $C$ is the representation cap and $S$ the aggregate weighted score. The fast-driver layout places nineteen parameter cells at free address $f$, a reusable six-cell color row at $f+19$, and color workspace at $f+25$. Further definitions specify retained B/C catalog headers, source-cover interfaces, reporting-prefix keys, suffix embeddings, terminal choices, positive frontier order, and frontier slots whose capacity depends on root raw mass. Program-interface predicates and resource functions support subsequent execution theorems.

theorems.theorem_title: Wanted-pair records, local-cover layouts, and stored reporting queries
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines the shifted wanted-pair output and its retained header. For pair count $c$, pair-array base $z$, and shift $\delta$, the four fields are
$$
[c,z,z+2c,\delta].
$$
It specifies lift-major A-key lists, pair decoding, physical owner catalogs, and the selected-color layout. Local-cover storage allocates coefficient rows, endpoint histograms, the support matrix, greedy workspace, and gathered schedule rows. Block-mask packing, selected-map flags, coordinate transport, valid reporting prefixes, and stored query values connect these arrays to reporting data. Light bodies cover source transforms, terminal endpoint preparation, canonical box sums, signed-box preprocessing, aggregate band scoring, and local parameter initialization.

/-!

The missing-subset masks are loaded from an actual array, and every
summand is produced by the verified box-query procedure. Signed
accumulator bounds follow from bounds on the original leaf weights.
The final theorem identifies the sum with the canonical powerset-card
sum whenever the mask array is an exact enumeration of that family.

namespace ThreeSum.LightBoxSum

open Light ThreeSum.SubsetAddress ThreeSum.LightPascal ThreeSum.LightSubsetAddress

variable {lim : Limits} {P : Program}

def boxValue {L : ℕ} (Q : Finset (Fin L)) (weight : Finset (Fin L) → ℤ)
    (U : Finset (Fin L)) : ℤ := SparseBoxes.boxSum (Q \ U) (SparseBoxes.queryFree Q U) weight

def partialSum {L : ℕ} (Q : Finset (Fin L)) (weight : Finset (Fin L) → ℤ)
    (missing : List (Finset (Fin L))) (j : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  ((missing.map (boxValue Q weight)).take j).sum














def roundBody (pBox : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  (Light.Stmt.seq
    (.call pBox
      [v 0, v 1, v 2, v 3, v 4, M ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 6) (v 10)),
        v 7, v 8]
      11)
    (.set 9 ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 9) (v 11))))

/-- Arguments: width, cutoff, Q cardinality and mask, missing cardinality,
number of masks, mask base, box-table base, polynomial scratch base. -/
def body (pBox : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  (Light.Stmt.seq (.set 9 (k 0))
    (Light.Stmt.seq (.for 10 (v 5) (roundBody pBox)) (.set 0 (v 9))))

theorems.theorem_title: Common-prime selection, retained transforms, and finite stage counts
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines a common modulus chain for all owner records. Starting from $q_0=1$, a nonempty prime pool supplies
$$
q_{r+1}=q_r p_{i_r},
$$
where $i_r$ is the first index minimizing the aggregate score at $q_rp_i$. It also defines retained prefix- and suffix-zeta stages, packed bucket setup, selected-map endpoint preparation, local greedy schedule indices, and original-color incidence interfaces. Row-major block coordinates, occurrence-bank order, forced-prefix decompositions, and raw bucket-product counts describe reporting inputs. Explicit wanted- and false-mass expressions and six principal work counts form the finite resource ledger; program bodies provide color-band construction, candidate scoring, coefficient preparation, and prefix-mask arrays.

theorems.theorem_title: Weighted owner catalogs, residue buckets, and reporting components
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines the aggregate score of a physical band-owner catalog $R$:
$$
\operatorname{score}(R)=\sum_{r\in R}\operatorname{block}(r),
$$
where an unflagged record contributes zero and a flagged record uses its three truncated bands. Catalog occurrences remain separate even when their values agree. The bundle specifies packed A-value, owner, and position arrays; finite owner-product domains; prime-pool generation; residue-bucket construction; common-offset selection; and weighted-score program bodies. It also defines local cover-matrix support bits, blockwise endpoint conditions, original-output decoding indices, raw reporting prefixes, child construction, sparse-box reads, arithmetic budgets, and the guarded hybrid caller assembly.

theorems.theorem_title: Rounded band scales, physical incidence domains, and transform passes
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines the rounded band size from the typed output count $T(n)$ and total inner size $\mu(n)$:
$$
g(n)=\left\lceil\frac{\lceil\sqrt{T(n)}\rceil}{2^{\lfloor\mu(n)/20\rfloor}}\right\rceil.
$$
It introduces owner-indexed A-incidence products, storage predicates for parallel incidence arrays, original-band sources, weighted modular scores, and raw encoding witnesses retaining original indices, arithmetic lifts, and schedule occurrences. Further objects include the integer cubic switch, trimmed-bucket scales, ordered global output records, and representation caps. Light bodies specify normalization with endpoint headers, execution of size parameters, query-subset enumeration, compact stage lookups, and layer-by-layer zeta passes, together with their resource expressions.

    (a : Fin L) (f : Finset (Fin L) → ℤ) (j : ℕ) (σ : State) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n r : ℤ) (μ' : ℕ → ℤ),
    σ = ⟨frame [L,cut,a.val,src,dst,maskBase,work,j,n,r],μ'⟩ ∧
    KeptBut μ μ' maskBase dst (downsetCap L cut) ∧
    TableAt μ' dst cut (stageValues μ dst j a f)























































































































































end ThreeSum.LightZetaPass

theorems.theorem_title: Integer block scales, occurrence encoding, and compact source routines
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines the integer block schedule from input length $n$. With $m=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (zero at $n=0$) and natural division, including $a/0=0$, its micro-size $u$, block count $J$, and total size $\mu$ are
$$
u=2\bigl(\lfloor\sqrt[3]m\rfloor/2\bigr),\qquad J=20\bigl(m/(100u)\bigr),\qquad \mu=Ju.
$$
It also defines physical A-incidence labels, packed band histograms and index buckets, occurrence-preserving global encodings, and ordered coefficient decoders. Light program bodies cover compact subset addresses, mask unions, greedy cover selection, local key arrays, coloring, modular triple counts, balanced offsets, and original-value leaf tests. Matching-key pair lists and the exhaustive original-triple fallback supply further specifications for later program composition.

def lowerBody : Stmt :=
  pass 4 (v 2) (v 1) (M (((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 0) ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.mul) (v 4) (v 3)))))

def lowerTime (m : ℕ) : ℕ := 25*m+6
























def upperBody : Stmt :=

          (M

              (k 1)))))))

def upperTime (m : ℕ) : ℕ := 100*m+6






























































def body (pDivide pLower pUpper : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  .ite ((Light.Cond.lt (k 0) (v 1)))
    ((Light.Stmt.seq (.call pDivide [(Light.Expr.op Light.Op.sub) (v 1) (k 1), v 2] 4)

primes to separate bounded nonzero differences. To use this same pool in

open scoped BigOperators

def moduli (C : Finset ℕ) : Finset ℤ := C.image (fun p : ℕ => (p : ℤ))




theorem prime_product_lower (C : Finset ℕ) (hC : ∀ p ∈ C, Nat.Prime p) :
    2 ^ C.card ≤ ∏ p ∈ C, p := by
  calc
    2 ^ C.card = ∏ _p ∈ C, 2 := by simp
    _ ≤ ∏ p ∈ C, p := prod_le_prod' (fun p hp => (hC p hp).two_le)

theorem product_gt_of_card (C : Finset ℕ) (hC : ∀ p ∈ C, Nat.Prime p)
    (M : ℕ) (hcard : Nat.log 2 M < C.card) : M < ∏ p ∈ C, p := by
  exact (Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self (by decide : 1 < 2) M).trans_le
    ((Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by decide : 1 ≤ 2) hcard).trans (prime_product_lower C hC))

theorem moduli_product (C : Finset ℕ) :
    (∏ p ∈ moduli C, p) = (∏ p ∈ C, p : ℕ) := by
  rw [moduli, Finset.prod_image]
  · simp
  · intro p hp q hq hpq
    exact Nat.cast_injective hpq

theorem moduli_pairwise_coprime (C : Finset ℕ) (hC : ∀ p ∈ C, Nat.Prime p) :
    (moduli C : Set ℤ).Pairwise (fun a b => IsCoprime a b) := by
  intro a ha b hb hne
  obtain ⟨p, hp, rfl⟩ := mem_image.mp ha
  obtain ⟨q, hq, rfl⟩ := mem_image.mp hb
  have hpq : p ≠ q := by intro h; subst q; exact hne rfl
  have hc : p.Coprime q := (Nat.coprime_primes (hC p hp) (hC q hq)).mpr hpq
  exact hc.isCoprime

theorem separates_nonzero (C : Finset ℕ) (hC : ∀ p ∈ C, Nat.Prime p)
    {M : ℕ} (hprod : M < ∏ p ∈ C, p)
    {z : ℤ} (hz : z ≠ 0) (hbound : z.natAbs ≤ M) :
    ∃ p ∈ moduli C, ¬p ∣ z := by
  apply Arithmetic.exists_aux_not_dvd_of_prod_bound (moduli C) z
    (moduli_pairwise_coprime C hC) hz
  rw [moduli_product, Int.natAbs_natCast]
  exact hbound.trans_lt hprod

    (hcard : Nat.log 2 M < (PrimeDensity.candidates y).card)
    {z : ℤ} (hz : z ≠ 0) (hbound : z.natAbs ≤ M) :

    fun p hp => (PrimeDensity.mem_candidates.mp hp).1
  exact separates_nonzero _ hprime (product_gt_of_card _ hprime M hcard) hz hbound

/-!
# The actual integer block schedule

All four size parameters below are executable natural-number functions.

namespace ThreeSum.Scales

open Filter Real
open scoped Topology

def inputBits (n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.log2 n

def microSize (m : ℕ) : ℕ := 2 * (Nat.nthRoot 3 m / 2)

def blockCount (m : ℕ) : ℕ := 20 * (m / (100 * microSize m))

def totalSize (m : ℕ) : ℕ := blockCount m * microSize m

def muZero (n : ℕ) : ℕ := microSize (inputBits n)

def mu (n : ℕ) : ℕ := totalSize (inputBits n)

def typedOutputs (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((256 * muZero n).choose (muZero n)) ^ blockCount (inputBits n)

def localSearch (C n : ℕ) : ℕ := 2 ^ (C * muZero n ^ 2)




/-- For integral `m`, `sqrt m + 1` is exactly `ceil(sqrt(m+1))`. -/
def windowExponent (m : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.sqrt m + 1

def primeWindow (n : ℕ) : ℕ := 2 ^ windowExponent (inputBits n)

def primeDepth (R : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.log (4 * primeWindow n) (R n / 4)

def primeLoss (R : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  32 * primeWindow n * 4 ^ primeDepth R n

def microHalf (m : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.nthRoot 3 m / 2

def localRadix (n : ℕ) : ℕ := LocalCoverBounds.localPrime (microHalf (inputBits n))

def radix (n : ℕ) : ℕ := localRadix n ^ blockCount (inputBits n)

def divisorBudget (k n : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.log (primeWindow n) (3 * n ^ k)

def scoreLoss (k n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (16 * (k + 2) * (inputBits n + 1)) ^ primeDepth radix n

    microSize m ≤ Nat.nthRoot 3 m ∧ Nat.nthRoot 3 m < microSize m + 2 := by
  have h := Nat.mod_add_div (Nat.nthRoot 3 m) 2
  have hr := Nat.mod_lt (Nat.nthRoot 3 m) (by decide : 0 < 2)
  unfold microSize
  omega

  exact (Nat.pow_le_pow_left (microSize_rounding m).1 3).trans

  have h := Nat.div_mul_le_self m (100 * microSize m)

theorem input_log_le_bits_add_one {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :

  rw [Real.log_pow] at hl

theorem bits_over_candidateCount_tendsto_zero :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (inputBits n + 1 : ℝ) / candidateCount n) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  have ht := windowExponent_tendsto_atTop.comp inputBits_tendsto_atTop
  have hu := ((tendsto_pow_const_div_const_pow_of_one_lt 3
    (by norm_num : (1 : ℝ) < 2)).comp ht).const_mul (4 * Real.log 2)
  simp only [mul_zero] at hu
  apply squeeze_zero' _ _ hu
  · exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun n => by positivity)
  · filter_upwards [actual_candidate_density] with n hC
    have hy := primeWindow_ge_two n
    have hyl : 0 < Real.log (primeWindow n : ℝ) :=
      Real.log_pos (by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 1 < primeWindow n))
    have hypo : (0 : ℝ) < primeWindow n := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 0 < primeWindow n)
    have hlower : (0 : ℝ) < (primeWindow n : ℝ) / (4 * Real.log (primeWindow n)) := by positivity
    have hbits : (inputBits n + 1 : ℝ) ≤ (windowExponent (inputBits n) : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
      exact_mod_cast bits_add_one_le_windowExponent_sq (inputBits n)
    have hs : (0 : ℝ) ≤ windowExponent (inputBits n) := Nat.cast_nonneg _
    have hdiv := div_le_div_of_nonneg_left
      (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) ≤ inputBits n + 1) hlower hC
    change (inputBits n + 1 : ℝ) / candidateCount n ≤
      4 * Real.log 2 * ((windowExponent (inputBits n) : ℝ) ^ 3 /
        (2 : ℝ) ^ windowExponent (inputBits n))
    calc
      (inputBits n + 1 : ℝ) / candidateCount n ≤
          (inputBits n + 1 : ℝ) / ((primeWindow n : ℝ) / (4 * Real.log (primeWindow n))) := hdiv
      _ = ((inputBits n + 1 : ℝ) *
          (4 * (windowExponent (inputBits n) : ℝ) * Real.log 2)) /
            (2 : ℝ) ^ windowExponent (inputBits n) := by
        simp only [primeWindow, Nat.cast_pow, Nat.cast_ofNat, Real.log_pow]
        field_simp
      _ ≤ ((windowExponent (inputBits n) : ℝ) ^ 2 *
          (4 * (windowExponent (inputBits n) : ℝ) * Real.log 2)) /
            (2 : ℝ) ^ windowExponent (inputBits n) := by
        apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right _ (by positivity)
        exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hbits (by positivity)
      _ = _ := by ring

    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, K * (inputBits n + 1) < candidateCount n := by
  have hsmall := bits_over_candidateCount_tendsto_zero.eventually

    exact_mod_cast Finset.card_pos.mpr hC
  have hKpos : (0 : ℝ) < (K : ℝ) + 1 := by positivity
  have h := (div_lt_div_iff₀ hCpos hKpos).mp hn
  have hNat : (inputBits n + 1) * (K + 1) < candidateCount n := by
    simpa only [one_mul] using (show (inputBits n + 1 : ℝ) * ((K : ℝ) + 1) <
      candidateCount n by simpa only [one_mul] using h) |> fun ht => by exact_mod_cast ht
  nlinarith

  have hdiff := log_difference_bound k hn
  have hk : (0 : ℝ) ≤ Nat.log2 (3 * n ^ k) := Nat.cast_nonneg _

  have hhalf := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hlog hk
  have hR : (Nat.log2 (3 * n ^ k) : ℝ) ≤ 2 * ((k : ℝ) + 2) * (inputBits n + 1) := by

  exact_mod_cast hR

/-!
# Concrete retained choices and the global radix encoding

The local choice type retains the occurrence of a map in the deterministic
schedule.  Repeated chosen maps therefore keep their representation
multiplicity.  Canonical integer lifts of their one-hot coefficients feed
the radix recursion, whose coverage and cap are instantiated here with no
local-cover assumptions.
-/

namespace ThreeSum.GlobalEncoding

set_option maxRecDepth 8000

open Finset
open scoped BigOperators
open LocalGraph LocalCoverBounds LocalHashMoments

def scheduleSize (h : ℕ) : ℕ := scheduleLength h (localPrime h)

theorem scheduleSize_eq_length (h : ℕ) : scheduleSize h = (localSchedule h).length := by
  rw [localSchedule_length]
  rfl

abbrev Occurrence (h : ℕ) := Fin (scheduleSize h)

def mapAt (h : ℕ) (i : Occurrence h) : Weight (512 * h) (LocalField h) :=
  (localSchedule h).get (Fin.cast (scheduleSize_eq_length h) i)











def Survives (h : ℕ) (i : Occurrence h) (e : Edge (512 * h) h) : Prop :=
  HashFamily.bucketSize (leftVertices (512 * h) h) (mapAt h i)
      (HashFamily.hashValue (mapAt h i) (left e)) ≤ localBucketCap h ∧
    HashFamily.bucketSize (rightVertices (512 * h) h) (mapAt h i)
      (HashFamily.hashValue (mapAt h i) (right e)) ≤ localBucketCap h

instance (h : ℕ) (i : Occurrence h) (e : Edge (512 * h) h) :
    Decidable (Survives h i e) := by unfold Survives; infer_instance

/-- A choice includes its schedule occurrence as well as its retained edge. -/
abbrev RetainedChoice (h : ℕ) :=
  {p : Occurrence h × Edge (512 * h) h // Survives h p.1 p.2}

def occurrence {h : ℕ} (c : RetainedChoice h) : Occurrence h := c.val.1
def edge {h : ℕ} (c : RetainedChoice h) : Edge (512 * h) h := c.val.2




/-- Sum of the canonical integer representatives of the selected symbol
weights. This is the raw integer sum before reduction modulo the prime. -/
def rawHash {h L : ℕ} (w : Weight L (LocalField h)) (s : Fin L → Bool) : ℤ :=
  ∑ i, ((w (i, s i)).val : ℤ)



























def rawLeft {h : ℕ} (c : RetainedChoice h) : ℤ :=
  rawHash (mapAt h (occurrence c)) (left (edge c))

def rawRight {h : ℕ} (c : RetainedChoice h) : ℤ :=
  rawHash (mapAt h (occurrence c)) (right (edge c))





































































def representations (h J : ℕ) (a b : ℤ) : Finset (List (RetainedChoice h)) :=
  Radix.representations (localPrime h) rawLeft rawRight J a b

def globalModulus (h J : ℕ) : ℤ := (localPrime h : ℤ) ^ J

def representationCap (h J : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (scheduleSize h * localBucketCap h ^ 2) ^ J





























/-- The integer difference contribution is determined by the equality

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
namespace Light
end Light

/-!
# A complete modular triple-counting procedure

Starting with three arrays of original signed integers and a positive modulus,
this fixed procedure computes its own power-of-two capacity, builds two padded
histograms, multiplies them with Karatsuba, folds the product into a correlation,
and looks up the residues of the A array. The result is exactly the modular
triple count used by the prime-score construction, including all multiplicities.
-/

namespace ThreeSum.LightModuloCounts

open Light ThreeSum.LightResidues ThreeSum.LightResidueHistogram
open ThreeSum.KaratsubaInterface ThreeSum.CyclicFold

variable {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {d : ℕ}

/-- Arguments: A, B, C, their three lengths, modulus, maximum length, scratch.
Local 9 holds the computed capacity; 10--14 are scratch-region pointers. -/
def body (pCapacity pHist pCyclic pResidues pLookup : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  (Light.Stmt.seq (.call pCapacity [v 6] 9)
    (Light.Stmt.seq (.set 10 ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 8) (v 9)))
      (Light.Stmt.seq
        (.set 11
          ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 8)
            ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.mul) (k 2) (v 9))))
        (Light.Stmt.seq
          (.set 12
            ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 8)
              ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.mul) (k 3) (v 9))))
          (Light.Stmt.seq
            (.set 13
              ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 8)
                ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.mul) (k 5) (v 9))))
            (Light.Stmt.seq (.set 14 ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 13) (v 7)))
              (Light.Stmt.seq
                (.call pHist
                  [v 1, v 11, v 4, v 6, v 9, v 13, v 14,
                    (Light.Expr.op Light.Op.sub) (k 0) (k 1)]
                  15)
                (Light.Stmt.seq
                  (.call pHist [v 2, v 10, v 5, v 6, v 9, v 13, v 14, k 1] 15)
                  (Light.Stmt.seq
                    (.call pCyclic [v 9, v 10, v 11, v 12, v 8, v 14, v 6] 15)
                    (Light.Stmt.seq
                      (.call pResidues [v 0, v 13, v 3, v 6, v 14, k 1] 15)
                      (.call pLookup [v 13, v 8, v 3, v 6] 0)))))))))))

def time (p nA nB nC U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  LightCapacity.time p + LightResidueHistogram.time nB (capacity p) U +
    LightResidueHistogram.time nC (capacity p) U +
    LightCyclic.combinedTime (Nat.clog 2 p) p +
    residuesTime nA U + LightLookupSum.time nA + 400

def space (free p N U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  free + 13 * capacity p + N + Nat.log 2 (U+1) + 2

def word (p N U : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  LightKaratsuba.wordBound (capacity p) N + 4*U + 4*p + 16 + N^3

























































































































































/-- Every procedure reference is tied to concrete syntax, including the
recursive multiplication closure. This structure contains no semantic oracle. -/
structure Procs (P : Program) (pMain : ℕ) where
  pCapacity : ℕ
  pHist : ℕ
  pCyclic : ℕ
  pResidues : ℕ
  pEmod : ℕ
  pHistogram : ℕ
  pMultiply : ℕ
  pHalf : ℕ
  pLinear : ℕ
  pFill : ℕ
  pLookup : ℕ
  main : P[pMain]? = some (body pCapacity pHist pCyclic pResidues pLookup)
  capacity : P[pCapacity]? = some LightCapacity.body
  hist : P[pHist]? = some (LightResidueHistogram.body pResidues pHistogram)
  residues : P[pResidues]? = some (residuesBody pEmod)
  emod : P[pEmod]? = some emodBody
  histogram : P[pHistogram]? = some (LightHistogram.histogramBody pFill)
  cyclic : P[pCyclic]? = some (LightCyclic.body pMultiply pLinear)
  multiply : LightKaratsuba.Procs P pMultiply pHalf pLinear pFill
  lookup : P[pLookup]? = some LightLookupSum.body


































































end ThreeSum.LightModuloCounts

end

theorems.theorem_title: Source preprocessing, bucket scatter, and output-record decoding
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines the composed preprocessing routines for colors, source hashes and histograms, local cover rows, trimming flags, and sorted reporting catalogs. Bucket-offset and scatter bodies use histogram prefix sums
$$
O_r=\sum_{q<r}H_q,
$$
where \(H_q\) is the number of original indices in bucket \(q\); their invariants track offset cells, insertion cursors and stored index segments. Further definitions specify header-based bucket views, original-value pair tests, radix digit arrays, occurrence-and-mask decoding, Pascal and subset-rank setup, cyclic folding, normalization, and band-candidate tables. Program-interface records and explicit time, word and scratch expressions support the separate compositional execution proofs.

  .ite ((Light.Cond.lt (k 0) (v 5)))

               (.set 0 (v 9))))))))
    (.set 0 (k 0))

theorems.theorem_title: Local hash schedules, positional keys, and arithmetic program bodies
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines the finite local hash-weight space and its greedy schedule. For half-size \(h\) and positive modulus \(p\), the prescribed schedule length is
$$
L(h,p)=320(2h+1)\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(p^2)\rfloor+1\bigr).
$$
It also introduces physical band-owner records, consecutive band partitions, prime-window candidates, indexed subset masks and weighted query-coordinate enumeration. The Light bodies cover positional coefficient construction, mask hashes, independent pair flags, signed histograms, lifted input keys, source residues, matching-key joins and output-index division. Karatsuba and merge-sort bodies, their procedure interfaces, result predicates and resource expressions provide arithmetic and sorting components for later composition.

  (Light.Stmt.seq
    (.set 9

        ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.mul) ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.mul) (k 2) (v 1))

    (Light.Stmt.seq

        ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 5)
          ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.mul) (v 8) (v 1))))
      (Light.Stmt.seq

set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
namespace ThreeSum.SubsetAddress

/-!
# Query-coordinate lists and weighted subset semantics

The coordinate list has one entry per set bit of the query. Its powers
form a compact weight table for the output-sensitive enumeration routine.
-/

namespace ThreeSum.QueryCoordinates

open Finset ThreeSum.SubsetAddress
open scoped BigOperators

/-- The selected coordinates among the first `j` scanned positions. -/
def positions {W : ℕ} (Q : Finset (Fin W)) (j : ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  (List.range j).filter fun i => i ∈ natPositions Q








@[simp] theorem mem_positions {W : ℕ} (Q : Finset (Fin W)) (j i : ℕ) :
    i ∈ positions Q j ↔ i < j ∧ i ∈ natPositions Q := by
  simp [positions]

theorem positions_nodup {W : ℕ} (Q : Finset (Fin W)) (j : ℕ) :
    (positions Q j).Nodup := List.nodup_range.filter _





@[simp] theorem positions_toFinset {W : ℕ} (Q : Finset (Fin W)) :
    (positions Q W).toFinset = natPositions Q := by
  ext i
  simp only [List.mem_toFinset,mem_positions,and_iff_right_iff_imp]
  exact fun hi => Finset.mem_range.mp (natPositions_subset Q hi)





def selectedPowers {W : ℕ} (Q : Finset (Fin W)) (j : ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  (positions Q j).map fun i => 2^i


















def weights {W : ℕ} (Q : Finset (Fin W)) (i : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (selectedPowers Q W)[i]?.getD 0












/-- Fixed-size sublists, interpreted as finite subsets. -/
def setLayer (xs : List ℕ) (k : ℕ) : List (Finset ℕ) :=
  (xs.sublistsLen k).map List.toFinset














theorem mem_setLayer (xs : List ℕ) (hn : xs.Nodup) (k : ℕ) (s : Finset ℕ) :
    s ∈ setLayer xs k ↔ s ⊆ xs.toFinset ∧ s.card = k := by
  constructor
  · rintro hs
    obtain ⟨ys,hy,rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hs
    obtain ⟨hys,hyk⟩ := List.mem_sublistsLen.mp hy
    refine ⟨?_,?_⟩
    · intro a ha
      exact List.mem_toFinset.mpr (hys.subset (List.mem_toFinset.mp ha))
    · rw [List.toFinset_card_of_nodup (hn.sublist hys),hyk]
  · rintro ⟨hs,hk⟩
    let ys := xs.filter fun i => i ∈ s
    have he : ys.toFinset = s := by
      ext i
      simp only [ys,List.mem_toFinset,List.mem_filter,decide_eq_true_eq]
      exact ⟨fun h => h.2,fun hi => ⟨List.mem_toFinset.mp (hs hi),hi⟩⟩
    apply List.mem_map.mpr
    refine ⟨ys,List.mem_sublistsLen.mpr ⟨List.filter_sublist,?_⟩,he⟩
    rw [← List.toFinset_card_of_nodup (hn.filter _),he,hk]
































































def missingSets {W : ℕ} (Q : Finset (Fin W)) (k : ℕ) : List (Finset (Fin W)) :=
  (setLayer (positions Q W).reverse k).map fun s => MaskDecode.decode W (maskOf s)

theorem decode_maskOf {W : ℕ} {s : Finset ℕ} (hs : s ⊆ range W) :
    natPositions (MaskDecode.decode W (maskOf s)) = s := by
  apply maskOf_injective
  exact MaskDecode.subsetMask_decode (maskOf_isMask hs).1

theorem missingSets_mem {W : ℕ} (Q U : Finset (Fin W)) (k : ℕ) :
    U ∈ missingSets Q k ↔ U ⊆ Q ∧ U.card = k := by
  have hn := (List.nodup_reverse.mpr (positions_nodup Q W))
  constructor
  · intro hu
    obtain ⟨s,hs,rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hu
    have hset := (mem_setLayer _ hn _ _).mp hs
    rw [List.toFinset_reverse,positions_toFinset] at hset
    have hr : s ⊆ range W := hset.1.trans (natPositions_subset Q)
    have he := decode_maskOf hr
    refine ⟨?_,?_⟩
    · intro a ha
      have hp : a.val ∈ s := by
        rw [← he]
        exact Finset.mem_map.mpr ⟨a,ha,rfl⟩
      obtain ⟨b,hb,hba⟩ := Finset.mem_map.mp (hset.1 hp)
      exact (Fin.ext hba : b = a) ▸ hb
    · rw [← natPositions_card,he,hset.2]
  · rintro ⟨hU,hk⟩
    apply List.mem_map.mpr
    refine ⟨natPositions U,?_,MaskDecode.decode_subsetMask U⟩
    apply (mem_setLayer _ hn _ _).mpr
    rw [List.toFinset_reverse,positions_toFinset,natPositions_card]
    exact ⟨Finset.map_subset_map.mpr hU,hk⟩









































end ThreeSum.QueryCoordinates

end

theorems.theorem_title: Subset enumeration, reporting frontiers, and bucket layouts
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines cardinality-layer and downset enumeration, mask decoding, Pascal-table storage, partial subset-transform stages, signed-leaf tables, and the ordered reporting frontier. For incidences \(I\), words \(w_i\), and natural weights \(a_i\), the prefix mass is
$$
M(k,u)=\sum_{\substack{i\in I\\\operatorname{take}_k(w_i)=u}}a_i.
$$
The frontier recursively extends prefixes and retains positive-query entries. Other definitions specify thresholded traversal budgets, block-source memory banks, stable residue-bucket positions and storage predicates, Boolean cover scores, coloring indices, and original-value bucket-pair scans. The bundle also supplies the remainder, logarithm, halving and merge routine bodies used by these components.

/-!
# Summing the actual dense-guard branches in physical slot order

The counter at slot i is the mass of slots before i. The expensive branch
is charged only when adding the current mass still fits the threshold.
These charges sum to at most that threshold, including when a later slot
crosses it. No bound on the mass of the crossing slot is required.
-/

namespace ThreeSum.SharedTraversalCosts

open Finset
open scoped BigOperators

def prefixMass (mass : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ := ∑ i ∈ range n, mass i

def guardedMass (mass : ℕ → ℕ) (threshold n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i ∈ range n, if threshold < prefixMass mass i+mass i then 0 else mass i


























def guardedBudget (mass : ℕ → ℕ) (threshold initial work n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i ∈ range n, (initial+
    if threshold < prefixMass mass i+mass i then 0 else mass i*work)

/-!
# The remainder of a division

emod(x, M, fr) returns the remainder of the integer x modulo M ≥ 1, a number in 0, …, M - 1.  The
language has no division: the routine writes M, 2M, 4M, … into a table at the free pointer fr as
long as they are at most |x|, subtracts them from |x| from the largest down where possible, and
corrects the sign (`emod_meets`).  With k = `emodRounds |x| M` doublings it takes `emodTime |x| M`
steps, a constant times k + 1, and k cells.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Light

variable {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {d : ℕ}
namespace Emod

/-- The local variables of emod: the arguments x, M and fr (the result replaces x), what is left
of |x|, the number of entries of the table, and the next multiple of M. -/
abbrev Arg : ℕ := 0
@[inherit_doc Arg] abbrev Modulus : ℕ := 1
@[inherit_doc Arg] abbrev Free : ℕ := 2
@[inherit_doc Arg] abbrev Rest : ℕ := 3
@[inherit_doc Arg] abbrev Count : ℕ := 4
@[inherit_doc Arg] abbrev Mult : ℕ := 5

end Emod

open Emod in
/-- One entry of the table: the multiple is written to the table and doubled. -/
def emodTableRound : Stmt :=
  (Light.Stmt.seq
    (.store ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v Free) (v Count)) (v Mult))
    (Light.Stmt.seq (.set Count ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v Count) (k 1)))
      (.set Mult ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v Mult) (v Mult)))))

open Emod in
/-- The table: M, 2M, 4M, … are written to the free pointer as long as they are at most |x|. -/
def emodTable : Stmt := .while ((Light.Cond.le (v Mult) (v Rest))) emodTableRound

open Emod in
/-- The last entry of the table that has not been tried is subtracted if possible. -/
def emodReduceRound : Stmt :=
  (Light.Stmt.seq (.set Count ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.sub) (v Count) (k 1)))
    (.ite
      (Light.Cond.le (M ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v Free) (v Count)))
        (v Rest))
      (.set Rest
        ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.sub) (v Rest)
          (M ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v Free) (v Count)))))
      .skip))

open Emod in
/-- The entries of the table are subtracted, from the largest down, where possible. -/
def emodReduce : Stmt := .while ((Light.Cond.lt (k 0) (v Count))) emodReduceRound

open Emod in
/-- The sign: the remainder r of |x| gives the remainder of x. -/
def emodSign : Stmt :=
  .ite ((Light.Cond.lt (v Arg) (k 0)))
    (.ite ((Light.Cond.eq (v Rest) (k 0))) (.set Arg (k 0)) (.set Arg (((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.sub) (v Modulus) (v Rest)))))
    (.set Arg (v Rest))

open Emod in
/-- emod(x, M, fr). -/
def emodBody : Stmt :=
  (Light.Stmt.seq
    (.ite (Light.Cond.lt (v Arg) (k 0))
      (.set Rest ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.sub) (k 0) (v Arg)))
      (.set Rest (v Arg)))
    (Light.Stmt.seq (.set Count (k 0))
      (Light.Stmt.seq (.set Mult (v Modulus))
        (Light.Stmt.seq emodTable (Light.Stmt.seq emodReduce emodSign)))))

/-- The number of doublings: the least k with a < M 2^k. -/
def emodRounds (a M : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.size (a / M)

/-- The time of emod, for a = |x|. -/
@[simp] def emodTime (a M : ℕ) : ℕ := 43 * emodRounds a M + 34




























namespace Emod

/-- What emod asks of the limits, for a modulus M ≥ 1, numbers up to V and the free pointer fr. -/
structure Pre (lim : Limits) (Mo V fr : ℕ) : Prop where
  mod_pos : 1 ≤ Mo
  space : (lim.space : ℤ) ≤ lim.word
  word : (4 * V + 4 * Mo + 16 : ℤ) ≤ lim.word
  free : fr + (Nat.log 2 (V + 1) + 2) ≤ lim.space

/-- The first i entries of the table are in place, and no cell below the free pointer has changed.
-/
def Table (μ μ' : ℕ → ℤ) (Mo fr i : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ j < i, μ' (fr + j) = ((Mo * 2 ^ j : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧ Kept μ μ' fr

variable {μ : ℕ → ℤ} {x : ℤ} {Mo V fr a : ℕ}










































































































































end Emod

/-!
# Logarithms, the cube root and halves, without division

Four routines on local variables only; none of them touches the memory.

* log2(x) returns ⌊log₂ x⌋ (0 for x = 0) by doubling (`log2_meets`).
* clog2(x) returns ⌈log₂ x⌉ (0 for x ≤ 1) by doubling (`clog2_meets`).
* cbrtCeil(n) returns the least s with s³ ≥ n, which is ⌈n^{1/3}⌉, by counting up
  (`cbrtCeil_meets`).
* half(h) returns ⌈h/2⌉ by counting up (`half_meets`).

Each of them is one loop that tries the candidates 0, 1, 2, … in turn.  Local variable 0 holds the
argument and receives the result, local variable 1 holds the candidate (`Arg`, `Cand`), and the two
logarithms keep a power of two in local variable 2 (`Power`).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Light

variable {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {d : ℕ}

namespace Logs





@[inherit_doc Arg] abbrev Power : ℕ := 2

end Logs

open Logs

/-! ## The logarithm, rounded down -/

/-- log2(x): the candidate is L, and the power is 2^(L + 1). -/
def log2Body : Stmt :=
  (Light.Stmt.seq (.set Cand (k 0))
    (Light.Stmt.seq (.set Power (k 2))
      (Light.Stmt.seq
        (.while (Light.Cond.le (v Power) (v Arg))
          (Light.Stmt.seq
            (.set Power ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v Power) (v Power)))
            (.set Cand ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v Cand) (k 1)))))
        (.set Arg (v Cand)))))

/-- The time of log2. -/
@[simp] def log2Time (x : ℕ) : ℕ := 14 * Nat.log 2 x + 12



































/-! ## The logarithm, rounded up -/

/-- clog2(x): the candidate is L, and the power is 2^L. -/
def clog2Body : Stmt :=
  (Light.Stmt.seq (.set Cand (k 0))
    (Light.Stmt.seq (.set Power (k 1))
      (Light.Stmt.seq
        (.while (Light.Cond.lt (v Power) (v Arg))
          (Light.Stmt.seq
            (.set Power ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v Power) (v Power)))
            (.set Cand ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v Cand) (k 1)))))
        (.set Arg (v Cand)))))

/-- The time of clog2. -/
@[simp] def clog2Time (x : ℕ) : ℕ := 12 * Nat.clog 2 x + 10






























/-! ## The cube root, rounded up -/



































































































/-! ## Halves, rounded up -/

/-- half(h): the candidate is r. -/
def halfBody : Stmt :=
  (Light.Stmt.seq (.set Cand (k 0))
    (Light.Stmt.seq
      (.while
        (Light.Cond.lt ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v Cand) (v Cand)) (v Arg))
        (.set Cand ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v Cand) (k 1))))
      (.set Arg (v Cand))))

/-- The time of half. -/
@[simp] def halfTime (h : ℕ) : ℕ := 10 * ((h + 1) / 2) + 10























end Light

end

/-!
# Merging two segments

merge(a, na, b, nb, dst) writes the merge of the na cells from a and the nb cells from b to the na +
nb cells from dst, within `mergeTime (na + nb)` steps (`merge_meets`).  The model is `List.merge`:

Nothing is assumed about the order of the two lists.  Numbers are only compared and copied, so their

@[expose] public section

namespace Light

variable {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {d : ℕ}

namespace Merge

/-! ## The pure side: one step of List.merge on the rests of two lists -/

variable {l r : List ℤ} {i j : ℕ}

/-! ## The program -/

namespace Merge

/-- The local variables of merge: the arguments a, na, b, nb, dst, and the numbers i and j of cells
already taken from the first and the second list. -/
abbrev ListA : ℕ := 0
@[inherit_doc ListA] abbrev LenA : ℕ := 1

/-!
# Enumeration of sorted-band triples through their quadratic owner set

Each owner is inverted with one binary interval lookup.  A final constant-size
test checks relevance and ownership.  No cubic list of triples is formed.
-/

namespace ThreeSum.BandEnumeration

structure Family where
  size : ℕ
  lower : ℕ → ℤ
  upper : ℕ → ℤ
  nonempty : ∀ i < size, lower i ≤ upper i
  sorted : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → j < size → lower i ≤ lower j
  separated : ∀ i j, i < j → j < size → upper i < lower j

namespace Family

abbrev Index (A : Family) := Fin A.size

def lo (A : Family) (i : A.Index) : ℤ := A.lower i
def hi (A : Family) (i : A.Index) : ℤ := A.upper i

def lookup (A : Family) (x : ℤ) : Option A.Index := do
  let i ← BinarySearch.locate A.lower A.upper A.size x
  if h : i < A.size then some ⟨i, h⟩ else none





















end Family

open Family

abbrev Triple (A B C : Family) := A.Index × (B.Index × C.Index)
abbrev Owner (A B C : Family) := (B.Index × C.Index) ⊕ (A.Index × (B.Index ⊕ C.Index))

def relevant (A B C : Family) (t : Triple A B C) : Prop :=
  Bands.Relevant A.lo A.hi B.lo B.hi C.lo C.hi t

instance (A B C : Family) (t : Triple A B C) : Decidable (relevant A B C t) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (Bands.Relevant A.lo A.hi B.lo B.hi C.lo C.hi t))

def owner (A B C : Family) (t : Triple A B C) : Owner A B C :=
  Bands.tripleOwner A.lo B.lo B.hi C.lo t

/-- Exactly one interval lookup for every candidate owner. -/
def candidate (A B C : Family) : Owner A B C → Option (Triple A B C)
  | .inl (j, k) => (A.lookup (C.lo k - B.hi j)).map fun i => (i, j, k)
  | .inr (i, .inl j) => (C.lookup (A.lo i + B.lo j)).map fun k => (i, j, k)
  | .inr (i, .inr k) => (B.lookup (C.lo k - A.lo i)).map fun j => (i, j, k)















































































































































end ThreeSum.BandEnumeration

/-!
# A rectangular Pascal table in the benchmark language

Every coefficient is built once by addition from the preceding row.
The row-major representation supports one multiplication and two additions
per later lookup. No recursive binomial-coefficient evaluation is used.
-/

namespace ThreeSum.LightPascal

open Light

variable {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {d : ℕ}

def tableSize (L : ℕ) : ℕ := (L+1)^2

def Table (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (dst L : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i ≤ L, ∀ j ≤ L, μ (dst + i*(L+1) + j) = (i.choose j : ℤ)

def rowBody (pLinear : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  (Light.Stmt.seq
    (.call pLinear
      [v 0, (Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 0) (k 1),
        (Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 1) (k 1), v 2, k 1]
      3)
    (.store (v 1) (k 1)))

def rowTime (L : ℕ) : ℕ := LightArray.linearTime L + 20

















































def buildBody (pFill pRow : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  (Light.Stmt.seq (.set 2 ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 1) (k 1)))
    (Light.Stmt.seq (.call pFill [v 0, v 2, k 0] 4)
      (Light.Stmt.seq (.store (v 0) (k 1))
        (.for 3 (v 1)
          (.call pRow
            [(Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 0)
                ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.mul) (v 3) (v 2)),
              (Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 0)
                ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.mul)
                  ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 3) (k 1)) (v 2)),
              v 1]
            4)))))

def buildTime (L : ℕ) : ℕ := fillTime (L+1) + L*(rowTime L+100)+100

def Inv (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (dst L i : ℕ) (σ : State) : Prop :=
  ∃ (r : ℤ) (μ' : ℕ → ℤ), σ = ⟨frame [dst,L,L+1,i,r],μ'⟩ ∧
    (∀ a ≤ i, ∀ j ≤ L, μ' (dst+a*(L+1)+j) = (a.choose j : ℤ)) ∧
      SameOutside μ μ' dst (tableSize L)

















































































end ThreeSum.LightPascal

/-!
# Computing all local-cover candidate scores

The input is a row-major Boolean cover matrix and an active-target vector.
This literal loop calls the checked Boolean scan once per row and stores
the negative count. A subsequent minimum scan selects the first maximum.
-/

namespace ThreeSum.LightCoverScores

open Light

def score (matrix : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) (active : ℕ → ℕ) (cols row : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  LightBooleanDot.dot (matrix row) active cols

def body (pDot : ℕ) : Stmt :=
  .for 5 (v 4) (
    (Light.Stmt.seq
      (.call pDot
        [(Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 0)
            ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.mul) (v 5) (v 3)),
          v 1, v 3]
        6)
      (.store ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.add) (v 2) (v 5))
        ((Light.Expr.op Light.Op.sub) (k 0) (v 6)))))

def time (rows cols : ℕ) : ℕ := rows*(LightBooleanDot.time cols+70)+6

def Inv (μ : ℕ → ℤ) (matrix : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ) (active : ℕ → ℕ)

  ∃ (v : ℤ) (μ' : ℕ → ℤ), σ = ⟨frame [src,activePtr,dst,cols,rows,i,v],μ'⟩ ∧
    (∀ j < i, μ' (dst+j) = -(score matrix active cols j : ℤ)) ∧
    SameOutside μ μ' dst rows

variable {lim : Limits} {P : Program} {d : ℕ}

theorems.theorem_title: Reporting accessors, scalar controls, and source-selection layouts
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines routines for indexed gathering, packed reporting keys, retained-catalog lookup, source-band selection, signed residue conversion, array scaling and signed-leaf evaluation. It includes compact subset-address calculations, support marking, independent trimming flags, and the scalar arithmetic of the reporting switch. For block count \(J\), depth \(j\), residual size \(r\), and candidate \(q\), two switch components are
$$
L=(291J+1000j)r^3,\qquad C=q\bigl(799r^2+q(72r+24q)\bigr).
$$
Additional definitions describe ordered radix decoding, modular triple counts, program relocation, source-header pointers and memory-fit conditions. Together they specify how reporting obtains stored data and computes its control values.

# Exact physical tuple indices for output decoding

The product enumerator is lexicographic: its first block is the outermost
choice. Repeated integer key values have no role in these index equations.
The recursive decoder takes the final coordinate by division and remainder.
-/

namespace ThreeSum.OutputDecodeOrder

open RadixKeyLists

set_option maxHeartbeats 1800000
set_option maxRecDepth 6000

variable {α β : Type*}

theorem getD_flatMap_uniform (xs : List α) (f : α → List β) (q : ℕ)
    (hf : ∀ x ∈ xs, (f x).length=q) (da : α) (db : β)
    {z r : ℕ} (hz : z < xs.length) (hr : r < q) :
    (xs.flatMap f).getD (z*q+r) db = (f (xs.getD z da)).getD r db := by
  induction xs generalizing z with
  | nil => simp at hz
  | cons x xs ih =>
    have hlen : (f x).length=q := hf x (by simp)
    have htail : ∀ a ∈ xs, (f a).length=q := fun a ha => hf a (by simp [ha])
    cases z with
    | zero =>
      simp only [Nat.zero_mul,Nat.zero_add,List.getD_cons_zero,List.flatMap_cons]
      exact List.getD_append _ _ _ _ (by omega)
    | succ z =>
      have hz' : z < xs.length := by simpa only [List.length_cons,Nat.succ_lt_succ_iff] using hz
      have hoff : (z+1)*q+r-q=z*q+r := by simp only [Nat.add_mul,one_mul]; omega
      rw [List.flatMap_cons,List.getD_append_right _ _ _ _ (by
        rw [hlen]
        simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one,Nat.add_mul,one_mul]
        omega),hlen]
      rw [hoff,List.getD_cons_succ]
      exact ih htail hz'





















def indices (m : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ → List ℕ
  | 0,_ => []
  | J+1,k => indices m J (k/m)++[k%m]

theorem indices_length (m J k : ℕ) : (indices m J k).length=J := by
  induction J generalizing k with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ J ih => simp [indices,ih]

theorem indices_lt {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (J k : ℕ) :
    ∀ a ∈ indices m J k, a < m := by
  induction J generalizing k with
  | zero => simp [indices]
  | succ J ih =>
    intro a ha
    rcases List.mem_append.mp ha with ha | ha
    · exact ih _ a ha
    · have he : a=k%m := by simpa using ha
      subst a
      exact Nat.mod_lt _ hm

theorem indices_getD_lt {m J k j : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hj : j < J) :
    (indices m J k).getD j 0 < m := by
  rw [List.getD_eq_getElem _ _ (by rw [indices_length]; exact hj)]
  exact indices_lt hm J k _ (List.getElem_mem _)

/-!
# Exact relocation of closed verified procedure libraries

Every procedure call is shifted by the same list offset. The structural
execution proof preserves the exact initial/final states, runtime, memory
addresses, values, and depth budget. It permits composition of independently
verified fixed programs without assuming a new implementation contract.

namespace ThreeSum.ReportingHostRelocation

open Light

@[simp] def relocate (offset : ℕ) : Stmt → Stmt
  | .skip => .skip
  | .set x e => .set x e
  | .store a e => .store a e
  | .seq s t => .seq (relocate offset s) (relocate offset t)
  | .ite c s t => .ite c (relocate offset s) (relocate offset t)
  | .while c s => .while c (relocate offset s)
  | .call p args x => .call (offset+p) args x

def program (prefixProgram P : Program) : Program := prefixProgram ++ P.map (relocate prefixProgram.length)

theorems.theorem_title: Array scans, reporting primitives, and resource parameters
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle defines Light program bodies for array arithmetic, Boolean dot products, histogram construction, table-lookup sums, minimum selection, natural powers, mask operations and one-hot hash evaluation. Its reporting routines include affine scans, original-value bucket tests, positive-count filtering and color-class extraction. For a natural count array \(c\), the selected-index list is
$$
[i\mid 0\le i<n,\ c(i)>0],
$$
in increasing index order. The definitions also specify argument and scratch layouts, loop invariants, time expressions, retained-memory conditions, source widths and endpoint bounds, and local-cover resource envelopes. These supply concrete bodies and specifications for subsequent execution contracts.

theorems.theorem_title: Arithmetic, subset transforms, and encoding parameters
theorems.natural_language_statement:
This bundle introduces the finite mathematical objects used by the construction: modular incidence counts, weighted histograms and correlations, local subset graphs, one-hot hash events, greedy covers, positional radix representations, and compact subset-mask addresses. For an integer-valued function on finite subsets, its zeta transform is
$$
Zf(Q)=\sum_{S\subseteq Q}f(S).
$$
The accompanying definitions include Möbius transforms, partial transforms, forced prefixes and sparse query boxes. It also fixes the rational exponent parameters, local prime and bucket-capacity choices, deterministic coloring family, original-triple indexing, and polynomial coefficient interfaces. These objects provide the common vocabulary for the later counting and machine-execution results.

/-!
# Exact arithmetic interface for the deterministic histogram construction

These are finite arithmetic and counting theorems.  They do not assert a
running-time bound or the existence of a word-RAM implementation.

namespace ThreeSum.Arithmetic

open Finset
open scoped BigOperators

/-! ## Guarded arithmetic-to-radix lifts -/















/-- The only three signed lifts queried by the algorithm. -/
def SmallLift (j : ℤ) : Prop := j = -1 ∨ j = 0 ∨ j = 1





































































































/-! ## The weighted false-count identity -/

























/-- Integer-valued divisibility is converted to a natural indicator. -/
def dividesIndicator (m x : ℤ) : ℕ := if m ∣ x then 1 else 0

/-- Number of auxiliary divisibility tests failed by an integer difference. -/
def missWeight (L : Finset ℤ) (x : ℤ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ l ∈ L, if l ∣ x then 0 else 1



































def modCount {ι : Type*} (T : Finset ι) (difference : ι → ℤ) (m : ℤ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i ∈ T, dividesIndicator m (difference i)

def weightedFalseCount {ι : Type*} (T : Finset ι) (difference : ι → ℤ)
    (L : Finset ℤ) (m : ℤ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i ∈ T, if m ∣ difference i then missWeight L (difference i) else 0










































/-- Pairwise coprime auxiliary moduli whose product exceeds the absolute
difference separate every nonzero difference.  No primality is necessary. -/
theorem exists_aux_not_dvd_of_prod_bound (L : Finset ℤ) (x : ℤ)
    (hcop : (L : Set ℤ).Pairwise (fun a b => IsCoprime a b))
    (hx : x ≠ 0) (hbound : x.natAbs < (∏ l ∈ L, l).natAbs) :
    ∃ l ∈ L, ¬ l ∣ x := by
  classical
  by_contra hnone
  push_neg at hnone
  have hdiv : (∏ l ∈ L, l) ∣ x := Finset.prod_dvd_of_coprime hcop hnone
  have hle := Int.natAbs_le_of_dvd_ne_zero hdiv hx
  omega

















/-! ## Exact early YES from per-original-triple representation caps -/

def fiberWeight {ι τ : Type*} [DecidableEq τ] (I : Finset ι)
    (owner : ι → τ) (weight : ι → ℕ) (t : τ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i ∈ I, if owner i = t then weight i else 0

/-!
# Finite numerical bounds for the local cover

The graph degree bound follows from exact finite cardinalities: the degree
is no larger than the number of vertices, while vertices times degree equal
outputs times representations per output.  This avoids any approximation
of factorials.  The prime-interval and normalized first-moment estimates
are stated explicitly in terms of the concrete binomial coefficients.
-/

namespace ThreeSum.LocalCoverBounds

open scoped BigOperators

def outputCount (L h : ℕ) : ℕ := L.choose (2 * h)
def vertexCount (L h : ℕ) : ℕ := L.choose h
def degree (L h : ℕ) : ℕ := (L - h).choose h
def groupSize (h : ℕ) : ℕ := (2 * h).choose h























































































/-- The exact expectation of the actual edge count, once its hash moment
identity has been proved. -/
noncomputable def mean (L h p : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (outputCount L h : ℝ) * groupSize h / (p : ℝ) ^ 2



































/-! ## A deterministic selected prime -/

/-- For positive `N`, this is exactly the integer ceiling of `sqrt N`. -/
def rootCeiling (N : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.sqrt (N - 1) + 1

theorem rootCeiling_pos (N : ℕ) : 0 < rootCeiling N := by
  unfold rootCeiling
  omega

theorem le_rootCeiling_sq (N : ℕ) : N ≤ rootCeiling N ^ 2 := by
  have hs := Nat.lt_succ_sqrt' (N - 1)
  simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one] at hs
  unfold rootCeiling
  omega

theorem rootCeiling_sq_le_four {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) : rootCeiling N ^ 2 ≤ 4 * N := by
  have hmono := Nat.sqrt_le_sqrt (Nat.sub_le N 1)
  have hpos := Nat.sqrt_pos.mpr hN
  have hlo := Nat.sqrt_le' N
  have hroot : rootCeiling N ≤ 2 * Nat.sqrt N := by
    unfold rootCeiling
    omega
  have hsq := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hroot 2
  nlinarith

/-- The interval is finite and explicitly enumerated; primality is decidable. -/
def primeCandidates (N : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (Finset.range (2 * rootCeiling N + 1)).filter
    (fun p => Nat.Prime p ∧ rootCeiling N < p)

theorem mem_primeCandidates {N p : ℕ} :
    p ∈ primeCandidates N ↔ Nat.Prime p ∧ rootCeiling N < p ∧ p ≤ 2 * rootCeiling N := by
  simp only [primeCandidates, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hup, hp, hlo⟩
    exact ⟨hp, hlo, by omega⟩
  · rintro ⟨hp, hlo, hup⟩
    exact ⟨by omega, hp, hlo⟩

theorem primeCandidates_nonempty (N : ℕ) : (primeCandidates N).Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hlo, hup⟩ :=
    Nat.exists_prime_lt_and_le_two_mul (rootCeiling N) (rootCeiling_pos N).ne'
  exact ⟨p, mem_primeCandidates.mpr ⟨hp, hlo, hup⟩⟩

def selectedPrime (N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (primeCandidates N).min' (primeCandidates_nonempty N)

theorem selectedPrime_spec (N : ℕ) :
    Nat.Prime (selectedPrime N) ∧ rootCeiling N < selectedPrime N ∧
      selectedPrime N ≤ 2 * rootCeiling N :=
  mem_primeCandidates.mp (Finset.min'_mem _ _)




theorem selectedPrime_sq_lower (N : ℕ) : N ≤ selectedPrime N ^ 2 := by
  exact (le_rootCeiling_sq N).trans
    (Nat.pow_le_pow_left (selectedPrime_spec N).2.1.le 2)

theorem selectedPrime_sq_upper {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) :
    selectedPrime N ^ 2 ≤ 16 * N := by
  have hu := (selectedPrime_spec N).2.2
  have hsq := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hu 2
  have hr := rootCeiling_sq_le_four hN
  nlinarith

/-- Integer ceiling of `4*(1+V/p)`, expressed using computable ceiling division. -/
def bucketCap (V p : ℕ) : ℕ := (4 * (p + V)) ⌈/⌉ p




























/-! ## The actual local parameters at `L=512*h` -/

def localThreshold (h : ℕ) : ℕ := outputCount (512 * h) h * 2 ^ (2 * h)
def localPrime (h : ℕ) : ℕ := selectedPrime (localThreshold h)
def localBucketCap (h : ℕ) : ℕ := bucketCap (vertexCount (512 * h) h) (localPrime h)

theorem localThreshold_pos (h : ℕ) : 0 < localThreshold h :=
  Nat.mul_pos (Nat.choose_pos (by omega)) (Nat.pow_pos (by decide))







theorem localPrime_prime (h : ℕ) : Nat.Prime (localPrime h) :=
  (selectedPrime_spec (localThreshold h)).1

theorem localPrime_pos (h : ℕ) : 0 < localPrime h := (localPrime_prime h).pos




theorem localPrime_sq_lower (h : ℕ) :
    outputCount (512 * h) h * 2 ^ (2 * h) ≤ localPrime h ^ 2 :=
  selectedPrime_sq_lower (localThreshold h)

theorem localPrime_sq_upper (h : ℕ) :
    localPrime h ^ 2 ≤ 16 * (outputCount (512 * h) h * 2 ^ (2 * h)) :=
  selectedPrime_sq_upper (localThreshold_pos h)
































end ThreeSum.LocalCoverBounds

/-!
# Executable binary search with a comparison budget

`upperSearch` finds the first array entry strictly above a query.  Its fuel is
logarithmic, and the proof accounts for the actual branches taken.  Array
accesses here are explicit function calls; a machine realization must still
implement those calls by bounded-address loads.
-/

namespace ThreeSum.BinarySearch

def upperSearch (f : ℕ → ℤ) (x : ℤ) : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ
  | 0, lo, _ => lo
  | fuel + 1, lo, hi =>
      if lo < hi then
        let mid := (lo + hi) / 2
        if f mid ≤ x then upperSearch f x fuel (mid + 1) hi
        else upperSearch f x fuel lo mid
      else lo
























def Partition (f : ℕ → ℤ) (x : ℤ) (n k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  k ≤ n ∧ (∀ i < k, f i ≤ x) ∧ (∀ i, k ≤ i → i < n → x < f i)







































def upperBound (f : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (x : ℤ) : ℕ :=
  upperSearch f x (Nat.log 2 n + 1) 0 n













/-- Return the interval containing `x`, with no scan through earlier bands. -/
def locate (lo hi : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) (x : ℤ) : Option ℕ :=
  let k := upperBound lo n x
  if 0 < k then
    if x ≤ hi (k - 1) then some (k - 1) else none
  else none






































end ThreeSum.BinarySearch

/-!
# The quadratic cardinal bound for relevant sorted-band triples

The proof is an explicit injection.  A relevant A interval either contains
the lower endpoint of a B/C difference interval, or its own lower endpoint
cuts that rectangle.  For a fixed cut, interval intersections inject into
the endpoints of the two families.

This file proves the combinatorial output bound and solution coverage.
It does not assign that bound to a cubic filtering implementation.
-/

namespace ThreeSum.Bands

variable {I J K : Type*}


















def Overlap (alo ahi : I → ℤ) (blo bhi : J → ℤ) (p : I × J) : Prop :=
  alo p.1 ≤ bhi p.2 ∧ blo p.2 ≤ ahi p.1

instance (alo ahi : I → ℤ) (blo bhi : J → ℤ) (p : I × J) :
    Decidable (Overlap alo ahi blo bhi p) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (alo p.1 ≤ bhi p.2 ∧ blo p.2 ≤ ahi p.1))

def overlapOwner (alo : I → ℤ) (blo : J → ℤ) (p : I × J) : I ⊕ J :=
  if alo p.1 ≤ blo p.2 then Sum.inr p.2 else Sum.inl p.1









































def Relevant (alo ahi : I → ℤ) (blo bhi : J → ℤ) (clo chi : K → ℤ)
    (p : I × (J × K)) : Prop :=
  alo p.1 ≤ chi p.2.2 - blo p.2.1 ∧ clo p.2.2 - bhi p.2.1 ≤ ahi p.1

instance (alo ahi : I → ℤ) (blo bhi : J → ℤ) (clo chi : K → ℤ)
    (p : I × (J × K)) : Decidable (Relevant alo ahi blo bhi clo chi p) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable
    (alo p.1 ≤ chi p.2.2 - blo p.2.1 ∧ clo p.2.2 - bhi p.2.1 ≤ ahi p.1))

def tripleOwner (alo : I → ℤ) (blo bhi : J → ℤ) (clo : K → ℤ)
    (p : I × (J × K)) : (J × K) ⊕ (I × (J ⊕ K)) :=
  if alo p.1 < clo p.2.2 - bhi p.2.1 then Sum.inl p.2
  else Sum.inr (p.1, overlapOwner (fun j => alo p.1 + blo j) clo p.2)


































































end ThreeSum.Bands

  ∑ s ∈ q.powerset, (-1 : ℤ) ^ (q.card - s.card) * f s

This file implements a dense, low-coefficient-first list algorithm. Its
correctness theorem is an equality of integer polynomials. The instrumented

/-!
# Finite sparse-query boxes

The largest-missing-element partition and the reusable box recurrence are proved
here as exact finite identities.  The accompanying cardinalities concern the
actual canonical box family, not the family of all arbitrary free-coordinate
subsets.
-/

namespace ThreeSum.SparseBoxes

open scoped BigOperators

variable {α : Type*} [LinearOrder α]

/-- A deterministic selection of the `t` largest elements, by successive maxima. -/
def largest : ℕ → Finset α → Finset α
  | 0, _ => ∅
  | t + 1, m =>
      if hm : m.Nonempty then
        insert (m.max' hm) (largest t (m.erase (m.max' hm)))
      else ∅

/-- A selected set consists of exactly the `t` largest elements of `m`. -/
def IsLargest (t : ℕ) (m u : Finset α) : Prop :=
  u ⊆ m ∧ u.card = t ∧ ∀ a ∈ u, ∀ b ∈ m, b ∉ u → b < a
















































/-- A box contains exactly the subsets between its required and allowed sets. -/
def BoxMember (flags free leaf : Finset α) : Prop :=
  leaf ⊆ flags ∧ flags \ free ⊆ leaf

/-- For a query set and a proposed largest-missing set, free positions lie below
every chosen missing position. -/
def queryFree (q u : Finset α) : Finset α :=
  (q \ u).filter (fun x => ∀ y ∈ u, x < y)

def QueryBox (q u leaf : Finset α) : Prop :=
  BoxMember (q \ u) (queryFree q u) leaf

















































































/-! ## Canonical free prefixes and the finite preprocessing family -/








































































































































































/-! ## The exact addition recurrence and query sum -/

instance (flags free leaf : Finset α) : Decidable (BoxMember flags free leaf) := by
  unfold BoxMember
  infer_instance

instance (q u leaf : Finset α) : Decidable (QueryBox q u leaf) := by
  unfold QueryBox
  infer_instance

/-- The signed sum stored in one box record. -/
def boxSum (flags free : Finset α) (weight : Finset α → ℤ) : ℤ :=
  ∑ leaf ∈ flags.powerset, if flags \ free ⊆ leaf then weight leaf else 0
























































































































































































/-! ## Number of query accesses -/

def explicitLeaves (q : Finset α) (t : ℕ) : Finset (Finset α) :=
  ((Finset.range t).biUnion (fun j => q.powersetCard j)).image (fun missing => q \ missing)





























































end ThreeSum.SparseBoxes
